extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, researchers, and members of the public inspecting a US design patent record
extracted.subtask_description: A US design patent document page (Google Patents) showing bibliographic metadata, figure descriptions, claim language, priority/continuity information, and legal-status/publication data for a package design with surface ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple views in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: FIG. 1 is a perspective view; FIG. 2 is a front view; FIG. 3 is a right side view; FIG. 4 is a back view; FIG. 5 is a left side view; FIG. 6 is a top view; FIG. 7 is a bottom view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent drawings should include the set of views necessary to fully disclose the appearance of the claimed design (e.g., perspective, front, right side, back, left side, top, bottom). The page exemplifies that each view is enumerated and described to show the claimed design from all relevant angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second embodiment drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: FIG. 8 is a perspective view of a second embodiment; FIGs. 9–14 are front, right side, back, left side, top and bottom views of the second embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple embodiments are claimed or shown, provide corresponding figures for each embodiment (full complementary views) and clearly label them as separate embodiments to illustrate variations of the design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings and shading conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent or application file contains at least one drawing executed in color; the grayscale shaded regions are regions of color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings are permitted; when color is shown, shading or other indicators (e.g., grayscale shading) may be used to represent color regions. Copies of patents with color drawings are available from the Office upon request and payment of the necessary fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken lines excluded from claimed design
rubrics_metrics.description: Broken lines shown in the figures described above are for illustrative purposes only and form no part of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements depicted in broken (dashed) lines are illustrative/environmental only and are not claimed as part of the patented design; use broken lines to indicate unclaimed subject matter or environment in which the claimed design is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim scope formulation for design patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim states: 'The package design with surface ornamentation, as shown and described.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent claims typically claim the appearance and are given scope by reference to the drawings and description. The singular, pictorial-focused claim formulation is standard: the claim covers the design as illustrated and described rather than functional features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic and priority/continuity information
rubrics_metrics.description: The record lists publication number, application number, priority date, filing date, inventor, current/original assignee, related parent applications, applications claiming priority, and family applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full bibliographic data and continuity/priority relationships (e.g., earlier filed design applications, continuations) so the claim to priority and family history is clear. This information is important for assessing priority date, related filings, and potential prior art windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-claim practice for design patents (as shown)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims (1): CLAIM — 'The package design with surface ornamentation, as shown and described.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents commonly contain a single claim that points to the drawings and description to define the claimed ornamental appearance. This example shows the single-claim approach typical of US design patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure legends and explicit labeling of embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure is captioned (e.g., 'FIG. 1 is a perspective view of a package design with surface ornamentation embodying the new design as shown, wherein the grayscale shaded regions are regions of color').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure legends should explicitly describe what each drawing depicts and may note special conventions (e.g., which shaded areas represent color). Clear captions help interpret the drawings and the scope of the claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications, citations, and prosecution history visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The record includes cited patents/publications, items cited by the examiner and third parties, 'Cited By' lists, publication dates, and related family documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide and maintain citation lists and prosecution-related documents to aid in assessing novelty, potential references, and the file history; visibility of cited references and citing documents facilitates prior art and landscape analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status and term information
rubrics_metrics.description: The page shows legal status ('Active') and anticipated expiration ('2030-03-22').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include current legal status and anticipated expiration/term to inform users about enforceability and remaining term of the design patent.
